claim: OpenAI secures agent network access through a sidecar egress proxy that enforces centralized allowlists and domain-scoped secret injection: the model and container only ever see credential placeholders, with raw secret values applied only at approved destinations and never entering model-visible context, reducing credential-leak and data-exfiltration risk.
stance_target: isolated cloud sandbox architecture for the triggers/infrastructure pillar, specifically credential isolation for autonomous agent workers
scope_conditions: OpenAI Responses API hosted container product, published March 2026
quoted_support: All outbound network requests flow through a centralized policy layer that enforces allowlists and access controls while keeping traffic observable. For credentials, we use domain-scoped secret injection at egress. The model and container only see placeholders, while raw secret values stay outside model-visible context and only get applied for approved destinations.

claim: Packing all input data directly into prompt context is an explicit anti-pattern; the recommended architecture stages resources in a container filesystem or SQLite-style database and lets the model query only the relevant rows/files via shell commands, which is faster, cheaper, and more scalable than copying full datasets into the prompt.
stance_target: naive full-context-stuffing is an acceptable data-ingestion pattern for agentic workflows
quoted_support: A common anti-pattern is packing all input directly into prompt context. As inputs grow, overfilling the prompt becomes expensive and hard for the model to navigate. A better pattern is to stage resources in the container file system and let the model decide what to open, parse, or transform with shell commands.

claim: Shell command output in an agent loop is explicitly capped per command (example given: 1,000 characters) while preserving both the beginning and end of the output and marking omitted content, preventing verbose terminal logs from consuming the context budget without adding useful signal.
stance_target: concrete output-bounding technique for context-efficient tool use in continuous-operation agent loops
quoted_support: To control this, the model specifies an output cap per command. The Responses API enforces that cap and returns a bounded result that preserves both the beginning and end of the output, while marking omitted content.

claim: OpenAI's Codex coding agent relies on native server-side compaction to sustain long-running coding tasks and iterative tool execution without quality degradation, and Codex itself was used as an early user/debugger of the compaction system during its own development.
stance_target: production precedent that context compaction is load-bearing infrastructure (not an optional convenience) for continuous agentic coding operation
scope_conditions: OpenAI Codex on the Responses API
quoted_support: Codex relies on this mechanism to sustain long-running coding tasks and iterative tool execution without degrading quality... Codex helped us build the compaction system while serving as an early user of it. When one Codex instance hit a compaction error, we'd spin up a second instance to investigate.

claim: Native compaction has the model itself analyze prior conversation state and produce an encrypted, token-efficient compaction item preserving key prior state; the subsequent context window consists of this compaction item plus high-value portions of the earlier window, and server-side compaction tolerates small context overages right at the limit rather than rejecting the request.
stance_target: technical specification of a production compaction mechanism for the cost/resource-optimization and continuous-operation pillars
quoted_support: Our latest models are trained to analyze prior conversation state and produce a compaction item that preserves key prior state in an encrypted token-efficient representation. After compaction, the next context window consists of this compaction item and high-value portions of the earlier window.

claim: OpenAI's Agent Skills follow a deterministic, lazy-loading sequence: fetch skill metadata, fetch and unpack the skill bundle into the container, then update model context with metadata and the container path -- only after this does the model progressively explore skill instructions and execute scripts via shell commands, mirroring progressive-disclosure skill loading seen elsewhere in the industry (e.g., LangChain Deep Agents).
stance_target: SOP-to-Agent-Skill pillar: lazy/progressive skill loading is a convergent industry pattern across OpenAI and LangChain
quoted_support: This sequence is deterministic: Fetch skill metadata, including name and description. Fetch the skill bundle, copy it into the container, and unpack it. Update model context with skill metadata and the container path. When deciding whether a skill is relevant, the model progressively explores its instructions, and executes its scripts through shell commands in the container.
